diagnostic_evidence.quote: The goal of this paper is to provide the first rigorous proof that, under suitable conditions, grade-wise training yields vanishing approximation error as grade number tends to infinity.
in which network parameters are learned from data rather than constructed analytically

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and introduction claim that grade-wise training (the per-grade optimization of Section 2) provably drives the error to zero. The theorems only assert the existence of analytically constructed affine maps with decreasing residuals. Nothing shows that these maps solve, or are reached by, the grade-wise optimization problems. The conclusion itself lists learned parameters as an open problem.

failure_location.quote: To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first rigorous theoretical guarantee that grade-wise training yields provable vanishing approximation error in deep networks.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the contribution as the existence/construction of a grade-wise ReLU scheme with monotonically vanishing residuals, and drop the claim that training yields it.
issues.overall_effect: The headline claim that grade-wise training is guaranteed to yield vanishing error is unsupported. Only an existential or constructive representation result is established.
issues.title: Claimed guarantee for grade-wise training is only an existence/construction result
issues.why_classification: The formal results are untouched, but an advertised guarantee is withdrawn. A comparable, weaker result remains.

The proof of Theorem 1.1 instead needs maps A_{n_1+1},... that are composed after the already frozen blocks A_1,...,A_{n_1} (5d-dimensional inputs). Theorem 3.1 as stated does not provide this. It would require the prefix to retain x, which is never stated or proved.

issues.failure_explanation: For f = 0 we have M_f = M_{-f} = 0, so no cubes arise and n = 0, contradicting n in N^+. Moreover, the claimed strict inequality reads ||f_2||_p < 0, which is impossible. The proof's case analysis never treats this degenerate case. Consequently, the proof of Theorem 1.1(ii) also breaks for f = 0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis f not identically 0 to Theorem 3.1. For Theorem 1.1, either handle f = 0 separately with constant output terms giving R_k = 2^{-k}, or exclude it. Observe that for f nonzero the residual never vanishes, since T_eps f <= 2^d eps M_f < M_f at maximizers.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem is false as stated for f = 0, and the proof of Theorem 1.1(ii) does not cover f = 0.
issues.title: Strict L^p monotonicity and n>=1 fail for the zero function

issues.failure_explanation: Sg vanishes away from the dilated cubes around the near-maximum set, so wherever g is nonzero there, |g - Sg| = |g| > (1-eps)|g|. For example, take d=1 and g(x)=x; at small x>0, Sg(x)=0. Only the sup-norm bound ||g-Sg|| <= (1-eps)||g|| and pointwise domination |g-Sg| <= |g| are established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claim with the established sup-norm contraction plus pointwise domination.
issues.overall_effect: This misdescribes the contraction mechanism as pointwise geometric decay. The formal proofs do not use it.

issues.failure_explanation: A positive eps-contraction only bounds |g^+ - Tg|, not its sign; the proof needs a,b >= 0. Counterexample on [0,1]: chi = 1-2x and Tg = g^+ + s_g(1-eps)||g^+||chi, with s_g = +1 if g(0) >= 0 and -1 otherwise. This T is a positive eps-contraction. For g = 1-2x, Sg = g + 2(1-eps)chi, so |g - Sg|(0) = 2(1-eps) > (1-eps)||g||.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Each such cutoff function can be implemented exactly by a shallow \ReLU{} network.

issues.failure_explanation: Psi is the average of trapezoids, so for d>=2 it equals (d-1)/d at points where only one coordinate lies outside [-r,r]. Gamma_Q is therefore supported on slabs, not on rQ. Hence the 2^d overlap bound and the step T_eps g = 0 outside the union of the rQ_i are false. At points of such slabs where g<0, T_eps g > 0 = g^+, so (C1) fails, and Theorem 3.1(ii) fails (|f_2| > |f_1| there). A genuine cutoff cannot be realized as claimed: in the paper's scheme each h_k is a one-hidden-layer ReLU function of x, since the trunk carries the identity. Such a function vanishing outside a small interior cube is identically zero in d>=2, because gradient jumps are constant along whole hyperplanes. For f a small interior bump, conditions (ii) and (iii) at k=1 of Theorem 3.1 are then incompatible, so the theorem is false for d>=2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must use a genuinely localized cutoff (e.g., ReLU(sum psi - (d-1))), which needs an extra nonlinearity. It must also re-architect the network realization, for example by pipelining across grades or using deeper blocks with changed width. Finally, it must drop strict decrease at the first grade.
issues.overall_effect: For d>=2 the main construction fails. Pointwise domination, the uniform contraction, and the width-5d single-block realization behind Theorems 3.1 and 1.1 and the corollary are all unsupported, and Theorem 3.1 is false as stated.
issues.title: Averaged Psi is not a localized cutoff for d>=2; C1 fails and localized cutoffs are unrealizable in the claimed one-layer-per-grade scheme
issues.why_classification: The core construction fails for every d>=2, and the stated architecture cannot realize the needed cutoffs. Repair requires new network constructions and changes the advertised scheme.
